title: The Sound of the Trumpet
english: The apostolic trumpet has summoned us to the feast, a trumpet Christ forged on the anvil of the cross, hammered by the gospel, fired by the Spirit, having smelted it to speak boldly of the old and new covenants—a trumpet it is no strange thing to proclaim, since we have drawn at once from prophetic and psalmic sources for this praise. Sound the trumpet!

For Andrew dispenses grace to all, lends the Spirit’s provision to everyone, enrolls all in the contest; he who was called first among all desires to be crowned last after all. Sound the trumpet!, since Christ’s mysteries, worthy of such a trumpet, must be carried to every land, and all owe it to proclaim yesterday to the nations. Sound the trumpet!

For the festal gathering is the sign of the intelligible warfare: there is need of battle and combat, of contest and grappling, of right hand and left arm to achieve the proposed victory. Sound the trumpet!, that by the voice you may overtake the foe and cast down the walls of mystical Jericho.
Let the sound enter the ears of the deaf, let it rouse from the dead those who are as good as dead, sleeping the heavy slumber of sin. Sound the trumpet in the new moon trumpet!
For now our life has become a new moon, having cast off the world’s rust, shaken off its wrinkles, been made fresh from old through the mystery’s initiation—on a notable day of our festival.

Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. But you, having heard the Lamb, proclaim the gospel of God; you have left behind the things below and the things above, and you busy yourself with many things, having let go of the net and having sent the net into heaven.
For do you not know that a net is not for catching fish, nor does a fishing rod draw? Your hand holds the earth and the heaven suspended.
What do you say? 'We have found the Messiah, the one called Christ'? Where then did you lose him, and how, and when? One finds the lost thing.
But how can the one who saves all be lost? How can the one who is present everywhere be found or spoken of? But Andreas knows what he says.

We have found what Adam lost, what Eve suffered damage from, what the cloud of sin has hidden from our eyes, what disobedience has separated, and what, though near and present, has been made to seem far away.
We have found the one to be sought after and…
